claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means do you live with him and are you the person who looks after him (providing food, clothing, and general care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me at the moment, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with money for his clothes, food, and things he needs regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex doesn't live with you, but you do contribute financially to his upkeep.

**Can you tell me who Alex currently lives with? For example, does he live with his other parent, another family member, or someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex lives with his mum, your ex-partner.

**Does Alex's mum currently claim Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex's mum doesn't claim Child Benefit for him.

**Is Alex's mum responsible for him - meaning does she look after him on a day-to-day basis, providing his care, food, clothing, and meeting his general needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she looks after him day-to-day since he lives with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

To complete my assessment, I have one more important question:

**Do you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit weekly rate (or an average equivalent amount) towards Alex's upkeep? The current Child Benefit rate for an only or eldest child is £25.60 per week (approximately £110 per month).**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £30 a week towards his upkeep, so that's more than the Child Benefit rate.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex based on what you've told me.

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 8 years old
- He lives with his mum (your ex-partner)
- His mum looks after him day-to-day and is responsible for him
- His mum does not claim Child Benefit for Alex
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week)

Let me make my assessment now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result

I'm afraid you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Child Benefit is paid to the person who is **responsible for the child** - this means the person the child lives with and who looks after them on a day-to-day basis. Since Alex lives with his mum and she is the one providing his day-to-day care, she would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

While it's positive that you contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit rate), financial contributions alone don't make you eligible if you're not the person Alex lives with and who is primarily responsible for his care.

**Important note:** Alex's mum would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex if she chose to do so, as she is the person responsible for him. She may wish to consider making a claim.
